easy.def: The front of your head, with eyes and a mouth.
examples: Wash your face.
She has a happy face.
A smile is on his face.

more.def: The front part of the head, where the eyes, nose, and mouth are.
examples: She washed her face before bed.
A big smile spread across his face.
The clown painted a funny face on the balloon.
It is a fact that cats purr.
A spider has eight legs; that is a fact.
Here is a fun fact about frogs.

more.def: Something that is known to be true and can be checked.
examples: It is a fact that the Earth goes around the sun.
Check your facts before you share a story.
The librarian told us an amazing fact about octopuses.

easy.def: To drop down to the ground.
examples: Leaves fall from the trees.
Rain falls from the sky.
Be careful not to fall.

more.def: To drop down from a higher place, often by accident.
examples: Snow began to fall softly outside the classroom window.
The toddler tripped and fell onto the soft rug.
Apples fall from the tree when they are ripe.
Leaves change color in the fall.
School starts in the fall.
We pick apples in the fall.

more.def: The season between summer and winter, when leaves change color and the days get shorter.
examples: In the fall, geese fly south in big V shapes.
We carve pumpkins every fall.
The air gets crisp and cool during the fall.

easy.def: Something you know or have seen before.
examples: That song is familiar. I know it!
I saw a familiar face at the store.
This street looks familiar.

more.def: Known to you because you have seen, heard, or done it before.
examples: His voice sounded familiar, but I could not remember his name.
The smell of baking bread was familiar and comforting.
Are you familiar with the rules of this game?

easy.def: A group of people who are related.
examples: I love my family.
Our family has a dog.
Her family lives near.

more.def: A group of people who are related, such as parents, children, and grandparents.
examples: My whole family gathers for dinner on Sundays.
The family next door has three children and a puppy.
A family of ducks swam across the pond.
She is a famous singer.
The famous writer came to our school.
This city is famous for its bridge.

more.def: Known and recognized by very many people.
examples: The famous painting hangs in a museum in Paris.
The town is famous for its delicious cheese.
He became famous after he climbed the tall mountain.
He ran far.
The moon is far.
Do not go too far.

more.def: At or to a great distance.
examples: The birds flew far across the ocean.
We hiked so far that our legs were tired.
Her house is not far from the school.
A far place.
The far side of the lake.
That is far from here.
We could see a boat on the far side of the lake.
The explorers traveled to a far country.
The shop is at the far end of the street.
A cheetah is fast.
My sister is a fast runner.
We took the fast train.

more.def: Moving at a high speed, or taking only a short time.
examples: The fast river swept the leaves downstream.
She is the fastest swimmer on our team.
A fast train can travel across the country in a day.
Run fast!
The car went fast.
She talks fast.

more.def: At a high speed or in a short time.
examples: The snow was falling so fast that we could hardly see.
Please do not talk so fast because I cannot write it down.
He rode his bike as fast as he could down the hill.

easy.def: A man who has a child.
examples: My father is tall.
Her father is a baker.
I help my father cook.

more.def: A man who has a child, or a male parent.
examples: My father reads me a story every night.
The father bird brought a worm to the nest.
She helped her father plant tomatoes in the garden.
It was my fault.
The mess is not his fault.
It is nobody's fault.

more.def: The blame or responsibility for something that went wrong.
examples: It was my fault that the cup broke.
Whose fault was it that we were late?
The accident was nobody's fault.

easy.def: Something that is not good about a person or thing.
examples: His only fault is being late.
She has few faults.
One fault of the toy is its weak wheel.

more.def: A weakness or flaw in a person or thing.
examples: One fault in the design was a loose handle.
Being late is his only fault.
The inspector looked for faults in the bridge.
Blue is my favorite color.
This is my favorite bear.
What is your favorite food?

more.def: Liked more than all the others.
examples: My favorite part of the book is the surprise ending.
Her favorite subject in school is science.
We went to our favorite park for the picnic.
